Practice guiding conversations so that people stay interesting rather than trying to talk much yourself. Pay attention to them. The benefits of this are two fold. Two, it allows you to learn what other people like talking about, what's really boring to listen to, etc and mixing in a bit of self awareness and a bit of forced confidence will allow you to learn how to eventually talk back to people and not just listen without as much trepidation of driving people away or not knowing what to say.

I used to be like this, and I honestly still prefer silence over conversation, but I've gotten a lot better at talking to people. The key is to start small and not care about sounding stupid, especially when talking with strangers. Attitude and appearance are half the battle. Bring confidence into your voice, look people in the eye when speaking with them, and give a firm handshake. If you can't stare at peoples' eyes for long periods of time while talking to them, stare at the space between their eye and ear. Try to talk about things you have in common. You don't have to be a know-it-all on the subject matter. In the case of strangers I'll take a guess on a commonality based on our location, the activity, and their appearance.

I'll practice conversing with strangers when I feel up to it. Here are some things I do:

*When I get into work in the morning, I say "Hi" or "Good morning" to everyone. I'll add a person's name to the end of the greeting if I like them. If it's someone I don't like, I'll address them as part of the group: "Hi, everyone." It doesn't hurt to throw in a smile and/or nod.

*If I see someone with a cool shirt or haircut or whatever, I'll say something like, "Hey, I like your shirt." You don't have to continue the conversation or even stand next to them.

*When standing in a checkout line at a store, I'll comment on something arbitrary to the person behind me. If it looks like they've bought ingredients for a single meal at the grocery store, I'll say something like, "Oh, are you making stew? I love stew, but I suck at making it."
